title: udlm_workingCopy — the sealed copy of the record
description:
The working record as it stood at the change, plus its resource-chain head. This is what makes a seal self-contained evidence rather than a pointer to state that may since have moved.

THE BRIDGE IS ONE-WAY, AND THE DIRECTION IS THE DESIGN. The seal embeds the record; the record never references the seal. So an operation never has to reach the ledger to proceed — records are unbounded in lifetime and compliance storage is not, and a dependency the other way would make every write contingent on a store that may be unreachable or aged out (ADR-059).

EMBEDDED, NOT REFERENCED, for the reason a receipt shows the amount rather than a link to the till: verification must be possible from the seal alone, by someone with no access to the live estate.

_schemaURL.description: OpenLineage: the schema defining this facet. Pinned to this file — a facet whose schema URL points elsewhere is a different facet wearing the same name, and the name is all a consumer has to go on.

record.description: The record's content at seal time, minus `integrity` — that is carried as `chain_head` below, because a digest cannot cover itself.

chain_head.description: The record's `integrity.head` at seal time. This is the join between the two families: a verifier walks pathway anchor -> seal -> resource chain -> audit log as one mechanical sequence, with no translation step where a mismatch could hide.
